1. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
2. use vstd::arithmetic::power2::pow2;
3. 
4. verus! {
5. 
6. // =================================================================================================
7. // Abstract models of external (arch-crate) frame-number quantities.
8. //
9. // `FrameNumber` is an opaque newtype defined in the (not-yet-verified) `arch` crate, and its
10. // maximum is the arch constant `FrameNumber::MAX`. Like `spec_page_size()` models the arch
11. // page-size constant, these uninterpreted functions model a frame number's integer index and the
12. // largest representable index in the spec domain. They are tied to the concrete exec values by the
13. // dependency contracts below.
14. // =================================================================================================
15. 
16. // The integer index (raw value) of a frame number.
17. pub uninterp spec fn spec_frame_raw_value(frame: FrameNumber) -> int;
18. 
19. // The largest representable frame index (models `arch::mem::paging::FrameNumber::MAX`).
20. pub uninterp spec fn spec_max_frame_number() -> int;
21. 
22. // =================================================================================================
23. // Derived spec helpers over the `PhysicalAddress` view (its `int` raw address).
24. // =================================================================================================
25. 
26. // The frame an address belongs to: `addr / FRAME_SIZE` (equivalently `addr >> FRAME_SHIFT`).
27. pub open spec fn spec_frame_number(addr_view: int) -> int {
28.     addr_view / spec_page_size()
29. }
30. 
31. // The base address of a frame: `frame_index * FRAME_SIZE`.
32. pub open spec fn spec_from_number(frame_view: int) -> int {
33.     frame_view * spec_page_size()
34. }
35. 
36. impl PhysicalAddress {
37.     // Well-formedness: the address has a representable frame number. This is exactly what makes
38.     // `into_frame_number` total (its internal `FrameNumber::from_raw_value(..).unwrap()` never
39.     // panics). `open` so callers' proofs (frame allocator, page tables) can rely on totality.
40.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
41.         spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number()
42.     }
43. }
44. 
45. // =================================================================================================
46. // Dependency contracts for not-yet-verified modules.
47. //
48. // `VirtualAddress` (the `sys` crate) and `FrameNumber`/`FRAME_SHIFT` (the `arch` crate) are not yet
49. // verified. They are given trusted external specifications so that the verified `PhysicalAddress`
50. // bodies can be translated. These declarations are placeholders: when the underlying modules are
51. // verified, their real specifications will supersede these.
52. // =================================================================================================
53. 
54. // Note: `VirtualAddress::new` now carries its own verified `#[verus_spec]` in the `sys` crate
55. // (`result@ == value as int`), so its placeholder `assume_specification` was removed — the real
56. // specification supersedes it.
57. 
58. pub assume_specification[ <::sys::mm::VirtualAddress as ::sys::mm::Address>::into_raw_value ](
59.     addr: VirtualAddress,
60. ) -> (result: usize)
61.     ensures
62.         result as int == addr@,
63. ;
64. 
65. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::FRAME_SHIFT ] -> (result: usize)
66.     ensures
67.         result < 32,
68.         spec_page_size() == pow2(result as nat),
69. ;
70. 
71. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::FrameNumber::from_raw_value ](value: usize)
72.     -> (result: Option<FrameNumber>)
73.     ensures
74.         value as int <= spec_max_frame_number() ==> (result is Some
75.             && spec_frame_raw_value(result->Some_0) == value as int),
76.         value as int > spec_max_frame_number() ==> result is None,
77. ;
78. 
79. pub assume_specification[ ::arch::mem::paging::FrameNumber::into_raw_value ](frame: FrameNumber)
80.     -> (result: usize)
81.     ensures
82.         result as int == spec_frame_raw_value(frame),
83.         0 <= spec_frame_raw_value(frame) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
84. ;
85. 
86. } // verus!

35. ///
36. /// # Description
37. ///
38. /// A type that represents a physical address.
39. ///
40. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
41. #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
42. pub struct PhysicalAddress(VirtualAddress);
43. 
44. //==================================================================================================
45. // Implementations
46. //==================================================================================================
47. 
48. impl PhysicalAddress {
49.     pub fn from_virtual_address(addr: VirtualAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
50.         // Delegate to the per-platform validator to support sparse physical memory layouts.
51.         if !crate::hal::platform::is_valid_physical_address(addr) {
52.             return Err(Error::new(
53.                 ErrorCode::BadAddress,
54.                 "address out of bounds of physical memory",
55.             ));
56.         }
57. 
58.         Ok(Self(addr))
59.     }
60. 
61.     pub fn into_virtual_address(self) -> VirtualAddress {
62.         self.0
63.     }
64. 
65.     ///
66.     /// # Description
67.     ///
68.     /// Constructs a [`PhysicalAddress`] from a [`FrameAddress`].
69.     ///
70.     /// # Parameters
71.     ///
72.     /// - `frame_addr`: The frame address.
73.     ///
74.     /// # Returns
75.     ///
76.     /// A [`PhysicalAddress`] associated with the given `frame_addr`.
77.     ///
78.     pub fn from_frame_address(frame_addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
79.         let raw_addr: usize = frame_addr.into_raw_value() << mem::FRAME_SHIFT;
80.         Self(VirtualAddress::new(raw_addr))
81.     }
82. 
83.     pub fn from_into_frame_address(frame_addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
84.         let raw_addr: usize = frame_addr.into_raw_value() << mem::FRAME_SHIFT;
85.         Self(VirtualAddress::new(raw_addr))
86.     }
87. }

89. // Verified conversions between a physical address, frame numbers, and MMIO addresses.
90. #[verus_verify]
91. impl PhysicalAddress {
92.     ///
93.     /// # Description
94.     ///
95.     /// Constructs a physical address from a memory-mapped I/O address.
96.     ///
97.     /// # Parameters
98.     ///
99.     /// - `addr`: The memory-mapped I/O address.
100.     ///
101.     /// # Return Values
102.     ///
103.     /// Upon success, a physical address associated with the given memory-mapped I/O address is
104.     /// returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
105.     ///
106.     /// # Safety
107.     ///
108.     /// Behavior is undefined if the provided memory-mapped I/O address is invalid.
109.     ///
110.     // Identity wrapping that deliberately bypasses the physical-RAM-range validator: MMIO
111.     // addresses may legally lie outside tracked RAM. On success the abstract address is unchanged.
112.     #[verus_spec(result =>
113.         requires
114.             spec_frame_number(addr@) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
115.         ensures
116.             result is Ok,
117.             (result->Ok_0)@ == addr@,
118.             (result->Ok_0).inv(),
119.     )]
120.     pub unsafe fn from_mmio_address(addr: VirtualAddress) -> Result<Self, Error> {
121.         Ok(Self(addr))
122.     }
123. 
124.     ///
125.     /// # Description
126.     ///
127.     /// Constructs a [`PhysicalAddress`] from a [`FrameNumber`].
128.     ///
129.     /// # Parameters
130.     ///
131.     /// - `frame`: The frame number.
132.     ///
133.     /// # Returns
134.     ///
135.     /// A [`PhysicalAddress`] associated with the given `frame_number`.
136.     ///
137.     // Total constructor: the result is the frame's base address, hence `FRAME_SIZE`-aligned.
138.     #[verus_spec(result =>
139.         ensures
140.             result@ == spec_from_number(spec_frame_raw_value(frame)),
141.     )]
142.     pub fn from_number(frame: FrameNumber) -> Self {
143.         proof! { lemma_from_number_no_overflow(frame); }
144.         let addr: usize = frame.into_raw_value() * mem::FRAME_SIZE;
145.         Self(VirtualAddress::new(addr))
146.     }
147. 
148.     // Total projection (under `inv()`): identifies the frame containing the address,
149.     // `self@ / FRAME_SIZE` (equivalently `self@ >> FRAME_SHIFT`). `inv()` underwrites the unwrap.
150.     #[verus_spec(result =>
151.         requires
152.             self.inv(),
153.         ensures
154.             spec_frame_raw_value(result) == spec_frame_number(self@),
155.     )]
156.     pub fn into_frame_number(self) -> FrameNumber {
157.         let raw_addr: usize = self.0.into_raw_value();
158.         // Bind `FRAME_SHIFT` once so the proof relates the shift below to the same value.
159.         let shift: usize = mem::FRAME_SHIFT;
160.         let frame_number: usize = raw_addr >> shift;
